analysis: Examined the two changed areas. (1) ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift:155 adds `await self?.acceptPendingClusterUpdateDrain(from: mailbox)` to the 250ms lifecycle monitor loop, next to the existing acceptPendingModelSwitch and acceptPendingAddonControl calls. The new function body, which presumably lives in ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain, is not in the supplied evidence. The mailbox is bound to ProcessIdentity, and the existing lifecycle request path checks request.isValid(for: identity) at line 149. Whether the cluster update drain request applies the same identity, owner-only and validity check is unverified. (2) ProviderLoop.swift:566-569 adds only two stored properties, clusterUpdateDrainID and clusterUpdateDrainTask, with no behavior. Nothing in this change makes the mailbox easier to reach or removes a control. The drain machinery (beginServingDrain, servingDrain.owner, lifecycleStatus) is unchanged. A new drain owner for cluster updates would need to interact correctly with beginServingDrain's owner checks at line 12, which currently exempt only .lifecycle and .addonHold from setting lifecycleStatus. It would also need to coexist with the TB-012 add-on hold and with T-059/T-060 availability concerns, in particular whether a mailbox writer can hold the provider out of routing without authentication or release it. The next pass should inspect ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain and the LifecycleMailbox cluster-drain claim and validation paths for peer and identity checks, bounded file reads, drain-owner arbitration, release on timeout, and the fail-open or fail-closed behavior. No concrete regression is identifiable from the supplied lines alone.
